strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with per-iteration scaling
strategies.desc: Uses 7 all-reduce operations executed sequentially, where each iteration computes block means, applies scaling, performs all-reduce, then unscales. This is the reference approach with 7 dispatches and minimal memory overhead. Represents the baseline with maximum dispatch count but simplest control flow.

strategies.name: Fused buffer preparation with batched all-reduce
strategies.desc: Consolidates all local scaling operations (mean computation, multiplication) before each all-reduce into vectorized operations over all blocks simultaneously, reducing kernel launch overhead. Still requires 7 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute dispatches from O(8*7) to O(7) by fusing block operations. Trades slightly higher intermediate memory for fewer local operation dispatches.

strategies.name: Pipelined all-reduce with overlapped computation
strategies.desc: Splits the 8 blocks into groups and pipelines all-reduce operations by initiating the next all-reduce while post-processing (unscaling) results from the previous one. Maintains 7 all-reduce operations but overlaps communication with computation. Represents latency hiding through pipelining at the cost of more complex scheduling logic.

strategies.name: Hierarchical reduction with two-stage aggregation
strategies.desc: Exploits the 224-rank topology by first performing all-reduces within node groups (if multi-node), then cross-node, potentially reducing effective world-size scaling per operation. Uses custom reduce-scatter + all-gather patterns to minimize data movement. May use more than 7 collectives but with smaller effective payloads per stage.

strategies.name: Block-wise independent all-reduce streams
strategies.desc:
Treats each of the 8 blocks as independent data streams and issues separate all-reduce operations per block (56 total: 7 iterations × 8 blocks), allowing hardware to parallelize communication across blocks. Dramatically increases dispatch count to ~56 but reduces per-dispatch payload from 2048 to 256 elements, potentially improving network utilization on high-bandwidth interconnects.

def r47_dd_meanabs_d7_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 256
    B = 8
    dtype = x.dtype
    
    # Initial all-reduce to get sum across ranks
    s = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # Vectorize operations across blocks to increase local computation
    for iteration in range(6):
        # Reshape to work with blocks more efficiently
        s_reshaped = s.view(B, S)
        
        # Compute all factors at once (vectorized)
        f = 1.0 + s_reshaped.mean(dim=1).abs()
        
        # Apply factors efficiently
        buf = s_reshaped * f.unsqueeze(1)
        buf = buf.view(-1)
        
        # Single all-reduce
        acc = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf)
        
        # Divide by factors
        if iteration < 5:
            acc_reshaped = acc.view(B, S)
            s = (acc_reshaped / (world_size * f.unsqueeze(1))).view(-1)
        else:
            # Final iteration: simpler division
            s = acc / world_size
    
    return s
